---
title: "Mixed models"
---

`fit_mixed_gaussian()` fits Gaussian linear mixed models, as `lme4::lmer()` does.
`fit_mixed_logistic()` fits a binomial logit model with one random intercept, as
`lme4::glmer()` does for that structure. It fits no other family or link, so it
has no `family` or `link` arguments. Both take an R formula with lme4's
bar syntax for random effects.

```php
Phit\fit_mixed_gaussian(
    string $formula,
    array|object $data,
    bool $reml = true,
    string $missing = 'drop',
    array|string|null $weights = null,
    ?array $start = null,
    int $maxEvaluations = 20000,
    float $tolerance = 1e-7,
    string $optimizer = 'bobyqa',
    float $objectiveTolerance = 1e-12,
): array;
Phit\fit_mixed_logistic(
    string $formula,
    array|object $data,
    string $missing = 'drop',
    array|string|null $weights = null,
    int $quadraturePoints = 1,
    int $maxEvaluations = 20000,
    float $tolerance = 1e-7,
): array;
```

## Supported structures

| Function | Random terms | Family and link | Fitting method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fit_mixed_gaussian` | `(1 | g)`, `(x | g)`, `(0 + x | g)`, `(x || g)` (uncorrelated), several terms such as `(1 | g1) + (1 | g2)`, interaction groups `(1 | g1:g2)`, and nesting `(1 | g1/g2)` | Gaussian, identity | REML (default) or ML (`reml: false`); BOBYQA (default) or Nelder–Mead (`optimizer: 'nelder_mead'`) |
| `fit_mixed_logistic` | Exactly one `(1 | g)` | Binomial, logit | ML by Laplace (`quadraturePoints: 1`, the default) or adaptive Gauss–Hermite quadrature with 2 to 61 points |

Any other random-effect structure, family or link throws code 1007. Random
slopes, several random terms, the Poisson and probit families, and REML are
not available in `fit_mixed_logistic()`. Random-effect terms in `fit_ols()` or
`fit_generalized_linear()` also throw code 1007.

## A random intercept and slope

The example uses [sleepstudy](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#sleepstudy) from lme4: average reaction times, in milliseconds, of 18 subjects over ten days of sleep deprivation. It reads the file by URL with phibble.

```php
use Phibble\DataFrame;

use function Phit\{fit_mixed_gaussian, fit_mixed_logistic, summary};

$sleep = DataFrame::fromCsv(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/datasets/main/csv/sleepstudy.csv',
);

$fit = fit_mixed_gaussian('Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject)', $sleep);
echo summary($fit);
```

```
Linear mixed model fit by REML
Formula: Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject)

REML criterion at convergence: 1743.6

Random effects:
Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev. Corr
Subject  (Intercept)   612.09   24.740
         Days           35.07    5.922 0.07
Residual               654.94   25.592
Number of obs: 180, groups: Subject, 18

Fixed effects:
            Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
(Intercept)  251.405      6.825  36.838  < 2e-16
Days          10.467      1.546   6.771 1.27e-11
```

- `(Days | Subject)` gives each subject its own intercept and slope, with a correlation between them. The fit uses REML, as `lme4::lmer()` does by default.
- The random-effects table gives each term's variance and standard deviation. `Corr` is the estimated correlation between a subject's intercept and slope.
- A subject's effects are its predicted intercept and slope relative to the average, shrunk toward zero. `tidy($fit, effects: 'ran_vals')` returns them with their conditional standard errors, one row per term and subject.

## Reading a fit_mixed_gaussian result

| Key | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `coefficients`, `std_errors`, `z_statistics`, `p_values`, `conf_int`, `covariance` | Fixed effects, with normal (Wald) tests and 95% intervals |
| `random` | One entry per random term, in formula order |
| `sigma`, `residual_variance` | Residual standard deviation and variance |
| `theta` | Relative covariance factors, as lme4's `getME(fit, "theta")` |
| `log_likelihood`, `aic`, `bic`, `n_parameters` | The REML criterion or the ML log-likelihood, according to `method` |
| `fitted`, `fixed_fitted`, `residuals`, `marginal_residuals` | Conditional and fixed-effects-only predictions and residuals |
| `method`, `optimizer`, `evaluations`, `converged`, `singular` | Fitting details |

Each `random` entry has these keys:

| Key | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `label`, `group`, `columns`, `correlated` | The term as written in the formula |
| `covariance` | The term's k×k random-effect covariance |
| `effects` | One row of conditional modes per group |
| `effects_cond_var` | One k×k conditional covariance per group, lme4's `ranef(condVar = TRUE)` |
| `group_labels`, `group_sizes` | Groups in order of first appearance after missing-value deletion |

- lme4 sorts groups instead. The estimates do not depend on the order.
- The fixed-effect tests use the normal distribution. lme4 reports t values without p-values, and packages such as lmerTest add degrees-of-freedom approximations. phit has no degrees-of-freedom correction.
- With few groups, Wald inference for the fixed effects can be optimistic.

## Singular fits

A random-effect variance estimated at or near zero, or a correlation at ±1,
makes the covariance singular. The fit returns with `singular` true and the
warning `random-effect covariance is singular or near singular` in
`diagnostics.warnings`. A singular fit usually means the random-effect structure is more complex than the data support.

## A binomial random-intercept model

[cbpp](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#cbpp) is lme4's data on contagious bovine pleuropneumonia: the number of new cases (`incidence`) among the cattle in each of 15 herds (`size`) over four periods.

```php
$herds = DataFrame::fromCsv(
    'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phpstats/datasets/main/csv/cbpp.csv',
);

$fit = fit_mixed_logistic(
    'cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ factor(period) + (1 | herd)',
    $herds,
    quadraturePoints: 10,
);
echo summary($fit);
```

```
Generalized linear mixed model fit by maximum likelihood (adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature, 10 points)
Family: binomial (logit)
Formula: cbind(incidence, size - incidence) ~ factor(period) + (1 | herd)

  AIC   BIC logLik deviance df.resid
194.0 204.1  -92.0    184.0       51

Random effects:
Groups Name        Variance Std.Dev.
herd   (Intercept)   0.4193   0.6475
Number of obs: 56, groups: herd, 15

Fixed effects:
                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
(Intercept)      -1.3992     0.2335  -5.992 2.07e-09
factor(period)2  -0.9914     0.3068  -3.232 0.001230
factor(period)3  -1.1278     0.3268  -3.451 0.000558
factor(period)4  -1.5795     0.4276  -3.694 0.000221
```

- `cbind(incidence, size - incidence)` gives the successes and failures for each row, as in `glm()`.
- `quadraturePoints` is lme4's `nAGQ`. The Laplace default (1) is fastest.
- More points approximate the likelihood more closely, which matters most for small groups and rare events.
- No number of points guarantees accuracy for every data set. Compare a few values when the estimates matter.
- A row may have at most 1,000,000 trials, counted as `cbind()` successes plus failures or as `weights`. Larger counts throw an exception with code 1007.

A `fit_mixed_logistic` result has the fixed-effect keys of `fit_mixed_gaussian` and these:

| Key | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `random_effects`, `random_effects_cond_var` | Each group's conditional mode (log-odds scale) and its conditional variance |
| `group_labels`, `group_sizes`, `n_groups` | Groups in order of first appearance |
| `random_intercept_variance`, `random_intercept_sd` | The estimated group variance and SD |
| `linear_predictor` | Log odds at the conditional modes |
| `neg2_log_likelihood` | −2 × the approximate marginal log-likelihood |
| `quadrature_points`, `integration` | The node count and `laplace` or `adaptive_gauss_hermite` |
| `gradient_max`, `boundary` | Largest absolute score at the optimum; whether the group variance is exactly zero |

## Prediction

- `predict()` adds each known group's random effects by default, as lme4's `re.form = NULL` does.
- `random: false` predicts at the population level, and the grouping columns can then be absent.
- A group the fit never saw throws code 1001 unless `allowNewLevels: true`, which predicts it at the population level.
- Mixed-model predictions have no standard errors, as in lme4.

## Matrix functions

`fit_mixed_gaussian_matrix()`, `fit_mixed_gaussian_intercept_matrix()` and `fit_mixed_logistic_matrix()` fit the same
models from numeric matrices and explicit random-effect designs.
`fit_mixed_gaussian_intercept_matrix()` is a faster path for a Gaussian random intercept by
ML. [Model contracts](reference-models.qmd) defines their inputs, the
optimizer controls and the convergence rules.
